title: React Testing Library & Vitest: Quick Revision
summary: Night-before revision of testing React components with React Testing Library and Vitest: role queries, user-event, async findBy, MSW fetch mocking, hook testing, and avoiding implementation details.

chapters.title: Testing Mental Model and Vitest Setup
points: RTL principle: test what the user sees and does, not component internals; the more tests resemble real usage, the more confidence they give
Vitest config: test.environment 'jsdom', test.globals true, test.setupFiles './src/setupTests.ts' inside vite.config / vitest.config
setupTests.ts: import '@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest' to add matchers like toBeInTheDocument and toBeDisabled
render(<App />) mounts into document.body; screen queries the whole document; RTL auto-cleans up after each test only when globals is true (otherwise call cleanup in afterEach)
Vitest vs Jest: use vi.fn(), vi.mock() and vi.spyOn() instead of jest.*; vi.mock is hoisted to the top of the file

chapters.title: Queries: getBy, queryBy, findBy and Roles
points: Three families: getBy throws if missing (sync), queryBy returns null (use for asserting absence), findBy returns a promise (async, waits up to 1000ms)
Plural variants getAllBy, queryAllBy, findAllBy return arrays; single variants throw if more than one element matches
Priority order: getByRole > getByLabelText > getByPlaceholderText > getByText > getByDisplayValue > getByAltText > getByTitle > getByTestId (last resort)
getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i }) matches the accessible name; also use level for headings: getByRole('heading', { level: 2 })
Debug with screen.debug() and screen.logTestingPlaygroundURL(); a failed getByRole prints all available roles

chapters.title: user-event and Async Assertions
points: const user = userEvent.setup() before render; every call is async, so always await user.click(el)
Core calls: user.type(input, 'hello'), user.clear(input), user.click(btn), user.selectOptions(select, 'a'), user.keyboard('{Enter}'), user.tab()
user-event vs fireEvent: user-event simulates the full interaction sequence (hover, focus, keydown, keyup, input) while fireEvent dispatches one raw DOM event
await screen.findByText('Saved') is shorthand for waitFor + getByText; use it when the element appears after async work

waitFor(() => expect(...)) retries the callback until it passes or times out; keep one assertion inside and never put side effects like clicks in it; use waitForElementToBeRemoved for disappearing spinners

chapters.title: Mocking fetch with MSW
points: MSW intercepts requests at the network level, so component code calls the real fetch unchanged; this beats mocking fetch itself
Handlers: http.get('/api/users', () => HttpResponse.json([{ id: 1 }])) from msw; the older rest.get and res(ctx.json()) are the v1 API
Server lifecycle with setupServer(...handlers) from msw/node: beforeAll(() => server.listen({ onUnhandledRequest: 'error' })), afterEach(() => server.resetHandlers()), afterAll(() => server.close())
Per-test override: server.use(http.get('/api/users', () => new HttpResponse(null, { status: 500 }))) to test error states; resetHandlers restores the defaults
Relative URLs need a base in jsdom, or use absolute URLs in handlers; in Node, fetch must exist (Node 18+) or the request never reaches MSW

chapters.title: Testing Hooks and Avoiding Implementation Details
points: renderHook(() => useCounter(0)) returns { result, rerender, unmount }; read the latest value from result.current
Wrap state-changing calls in act(() => { result.current.increment() }) so React flushes updates before you assert
Hooks needing context: renderHook(() => useAuth(), { wrapper: AuthProvider }); pass initialProps with rerender to test changing props
Prefer testing a hook through a component when it is only used by one component; use renderHook for reusable hooks with their own contract

Implementation details to avoid: asserting on state values, calling instance methods, snapshot-testing whole trees, shallow rendering, querying by CSS class or test id; assert visible text, roles and behavior so refactors do not break tests

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: Testing Library Essentials
points: Setup: environment 'jsdom', globals true, setupFiles with '@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest'
Query pick: getBy for present, queryBy for absent (expect(...).not.toBeInTheDocument()), findBy for async
Interaction: const user = userEvent.setup(); await user.click(...); await user.type(...)
MSW skeleton: setupServer, listen in beforeAll, resetHandlers in afterEach, close in afterAll, server.use for per-test overrides
Hooks: renderHook + act + result.current; wrapper option for providers
